from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Complex waves hide simple building blocks.", "A meow is just many sines.", "Watch these waves add up perfectly.", "Separate the waves into simple parts.", "Reconstructing the signal is our goal."]
        self.setup_layout("Intuitive Hook: The Symphony of Waves", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create elements
        wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(3*x) + 0.3 * np.sin(5*x), color="#3498DB")
        label = Text("Frequency Component", font_size=20, color="#ECF0F1")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#3498DB")
        self.place_in_area(wave, 'B2', 'D5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(wave))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#E74C3C")
        self.play(wave.animate.set_color("#E74C3C"), run_time=1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#ECF0F1")
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'E3', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Write(label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#2ECC71")
        self.play(wave.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.5), run_time=1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#F1C40F")
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Core Formula: The Fourier Recipe", [
            "The Fourier series is a mathematical recipe.", 
            "We sum sine and cosine components.", 
            "Weights determine the contribution of each.", 
            "Ingredients create a complex target shape.", 
            "Mixing waves builds the final function."
        ])
        
        # Define Formula
        fourier_formula = MathTex(
            "f(x) = \\frac{a_0}{2} + \\sum_{n=1}^{\\infty} (a_n \\cos(nx) + b_n \\sin(nx))",
            font_size=36
        )
        self.place_in_area(fourier_formula, 'B2', 'C5', scale_factor=1.2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.play(Write(fourier_formula))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#E67E22")
        self.play(fourier_formula[0][7:9].animate.set_color("#E67E22"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#3498DB")
        self.play(
            fourier_formula[0][2:4].animate.set_color("#3498DB"),
            fourier_formula[0][11:13].animate.set_color("#3498DB"),
            fourier_formula[0][18:20].animate.set_color("#3498DB")
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#9B59B6")
        # Visualizing component signals (placeholder: simple sine wave representation)
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 6, 1], y_range=[-1, 1, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        wave = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x), color="#9B59B6")
        component = VGroup(axes, wave)
        self.place_in_area(component, 'D2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(component))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(
            fourier_formula.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            component.animate.set_color(GREEN)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Integrals extract our specific frequency coefficients.", 
                         "The filter isolates one harmonic wave.", 
                         "See the amplitude emerge from integration."]
        
        self.setup_layout("Calculating the Coefficients", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create Math elements
        an_formula = MathTex(r"a_n = \frac{2}{T} \int_0^T f(t) \cos(n \omega t) dt", font_size=36)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#2ECC71")
        self.place_in_area(an_formula, "B2", "C5", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(an_formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#F1C40F")
        # Highlight dt part
        differential = an_formula[0][-2:]
        self.play(differential.animate.set_color("#F1C40F"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#ECF0F1")
        result_text = Text("Amplitude emerges", font_size=24, color="#E74C3C")
        self.place_at_grid(result_text, "E3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(result_text))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Digital Signal Processor", [
            "Fourier series power modern digital compression.",
            "Adjusting coefficients filters audio noise away.",
            "Equalizers show these principles in action."
        ])
        
        # --- Animation Content ---
        # Data points for waveform
        points = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.05, color="#3498DB") for _ in range(20)])
        for i, p in enumerate(points):
            p.move_to(np.array([-2.5 + i * 0.3, 0.5 * np.sin(i * 0.5), 0]))
            
        # Fourier curve
        fourier_curve = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(x), x_range=[-3, 3], color="#E74C3C")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#3498DB")
        self.play(Create(points))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#E74C3C")
        self.place_in_area(fourier_curve, 'B2', 'D5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(fourier_curve))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#F1C40F")
        error_arrows = VGroup(*[
            Arrow(start=points[i].get_center(), end=fourier_curve.point_from_proportion(i/19), color=WHITE, buff=0.1, tip_length=0.1)
            for i in range(0, 20, 2)
        ])
        self.play(Create(error_arrows))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Magic of Pure Fourier Series: Breaking Down Waves

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Symphony of Waves
sections.content: Introduce the core intuition: any complex periodic signal (like a cat's meow or a musical note) can be reconstructed by summing simple sine and cosine waves.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Cat Meow' waveform on an oscilloscope being broken down into 3 basic sine waves of different frequencies.

sections.title: Prerequisite Refresher: Orthogonality
sections.content: Briefly define periodicity (T) and the concept of basis functions. Emphasize that sine and cosine are 'orthogonal'—like perpendicular axes in space, they don't interfere with each other.
sections.example: Animation showing two sine waves (sin(x) and sin(2x)) multiplying and integrating to zero over a period, demonstrating their independence.

sections.title: The Core Formula: The Fourier Recipe
sections.content: Present the Fourier Series expansion: f(x) = a0/2 + Σ(an*cos(nx) + bn*sin(nx)). Explain the roles of 'an' and 'bn' as the 'ingredients' or 'weights' that determine the contribution of each frequency.
sections.example: A recipe card graphic where 'ingredients' (sine/cosine waves) are multiplied by their specific 'weights' (coefficients) to bake a Square Wave.

sections.title: Calculating the Coefficients
sections.content: Explain the integration method to extract coefficients. Connect the math to the visual: the integral acts as a 'filter' that highlights the specific frequency component.
sections.example: An animation showing a 'sliding window' integral formula pulling out the specific amplitude for a 3rd harmonic component.

sections.title: Application: The Digital Signal Processor
sections.content: Conclude with real-world utility: Fourier series allow devices to compress audio (MP3) or filter out background noise.
sections.example: A visual demonstration of an 'Equalizer' interface where moving sliders adjusts the 'an' and 'bn' coefficients to change the sound profile of a guitar.
